- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.67) and recent history shows upward momentum — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially <0.33) or shows strong downward momentum — increase forecast lows to avoid under-shock.
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes in sentiment — cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below recent high or adjust downward 2–3 days post-spike.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >15% above 30d moving average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- Lagged overreaction: if forecast is >10% above true outcome 3–5 days prior, adjust downward 2–5% for next period.
- Sentiment-driven bias: if sentiment >0.75 for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 3–5% to avoid overconfidence in trend.
- Horizon-specific: 30d forecasts are prone to over-optimism — apply 5–10% downward bias if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.
